name: Thyrotoxicosis factitia with thyrotoxic crisis or storm
description: Thyrotoxicosis factitia is a condition of thyrotoxicosis caused by the ingestion of exogenous thyroid hormone. It can be the result of mistaken ingestion of excess drugs, such as levothyroxine and triiodothyronine, or as a symptom of Munchausen syndrome.

red_flags.condition: [LLM DRAFT] Presentation with signs of thyroid storm including severe hyperthermia, tachycardia out of proportion to fever, altered mental status, and gastrointestinal dysfunction in a patient with thyrotoxicosis factitia.

questions.text: [LLM DRAFT] Are you experiencing a dangerously high fever, severe confusion, or a racing heartbeat while taking thyroid hormone medications in excessive amounts?
questions.purpose: Screens for severe thyrotoxic crisis symptoms linked to excessive thyroid hormone use

questions.text: [LLM DRAFT] Have you recently ingested very high doses of thyroid hormone supplements or medications?
questions.purpose: Screens for the exogenous source of thyroid hormone characteristic of factitious thyrotoxicosis

differentials.distinguishing_feature: [LLM DRAFT] Presents with hyperthyroid storm symptoms due to endogenous overproduction rather than exogenous hormone ingestion.
[LLM DRAFT] Presents with biochemical thyrotoxicosis from exogenous hormone use but lacks the life-threatening systemic decompensation of a storm.
[LLM DRAFT] Features acute life-threatening storm symptoms where the specific endogenous or exogenous etiology has not yet been determined.

icd10_official_description: Thyrotoxicosis factitia with thyrotoxic crisis or storm
